problem_statement: Technext Small Apps is a directly runnable static Bootstrap app-landing marketing website (a homepage plus about, contact, FAQ and blog routes sharing a fixed top navigation with nested dropdowns, a hero CTA, feature blocks, a video/testimonial section, a contact address/form and a footer, with one shared js/script.js and local logo/feature/testimonial imagery). The marketing team wants the homepage feature section rebuilt into a Feature Finder: an interactive discipline filter (All / Design / Data / Workflow) sitting above a responsive grid of six real feature cards (Easy Prototyping, Art Direction, Sensor Bridge, Insight Charts, Strategist, Task Relay), each tagged with a discipline, plus a live count readout that reads 'Showing N of 6 · <discipline>'. Clicking a discipline tab filters the grid to the matching cards AND updates the readout count and label; clicking All restores all six. The same Feature Finder block must also appear near the bottom of the About and Contact routes so the capability browser is reachable across the marketing site. The homepage already carries the Feature Finder markup (a .featfinder section with an h2 'Find the right Small Apps feature', a .featfinder__bar of four .featfinder__tab buttons, a .featfinder__readout, and a .featfinder__grid of six .featfinder__card tiles). Two defects must be repaired: (1) a responsive layout defect — the filter bar and grid are pinned to fixed widths so the finder region overflows a 390px phone horizontally; the reference lets the bar wrap and the grid collapse to fewer columns so the homepage has no horizontal scroll while desktop and tablet stay unchanged; and (2) the finder must appear on the About and Contact routes, not the homepage alone. The filter interaction itself (cards re-filter and the readout recomputes to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Data' etc.) must work live on every click.
required_content: Keep the homepage Feature Finder (the .featfinder section with h2 'Find the right Small Apps feature', four discipline tabs All/Design/Data/Workflow, a live readout, and six feature cards) in place of the original services section.

Wire the discipline filter so clicking a tab shows only the matching cards and updates the readout to 'Showing N of 6 · <discipline>' (All restores 'Showing 6 of 6 · All disciplines'); the readout count and label must recompute on every click, not stay frozen.

Lay the Feature Finder out responsively so the homepage has no horizontal scroll on a 390px phone: the tab bar wraps and the card grid collapses to fewer columns instead of sitting at a fixed width; keep the desktop and tablet layouts and the card legibility unchanged.
Render the same Feature Finder block near the bottom of the About and Contact routes so the capability browser is reachable across the marketing site.

Preserve the Small Apps content, the shared top navigation, the hero, video/testimonial section, the contact address/form, the FAQ route and the local imagery; introduce no console pageerrors or failed network requests and add no framework, package manager, backend or generated build output.
design_constraints: Keep the Feature Finder where the marketing page hosts its capability browse (the homepage feature section, and near the bottom of About and Contact); do not move it to a new route or replace the hero, video, testimonial or footer.
Fix the overflow only by making the finder responsive (wrap the tab bar, collapse the grid, min-width:0 on the cards); do not delete the finder, drop cards or hide it to dodge the overflow.

Keep the six cards legible and non-overlapping: readable heading/body text on a light card, tidy grid gaps — do not shingle the cards into an overlapping pile or drop text contrast to the point of being unreadable.
Fit the Small Apps visual language: Bootstrap grid, white cards, soft shadows, #2e7eed blue accents, rounded pill tabs.

Keep the implementation static inside the current HTML/Bootstrap/CSS/vanilla-JS structure; do not add a framework, package manager, backend, remote image replacement or hidden-only text, and introduce no console pageerrors or failed network requests.
state_constraints: desktop_home renders the Feature Finder (h2, four discipline tabs, readout, six legible cards) within the 1440px viewport with no horizontal overflow.
mobile_home renders the homepage within a 390px phone viewport with no horizontal scroll after the responsive fix (the overflow discriminator).
tablet_home renders the 834px tablet viewport with no horizontal overflow beyond tolerance.
desktop_home_data clicks the Data discipline tab and verifies the readout recomputes to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Data' (changed from the pre-click 'Showing 6 of 6 · All disciplines').
desktop_about verifies the About route renders the Feature Finder block (cross-page presence).
desktop_contact verifies the Contact route renders the Feature Finder block and its address/form.
desktop_faq verifies the FAQ route still renders after the change.

change_completion: The homepage renders the Feature Finder (h2 'Find the right Small Apps feature', four discipline tabs, a readout and six feature cards) in place of the original services section.
Clicking a discipline tab filters the grid to the matching cards and recomputes the readout to 'Showing N of 6 · <discipline>'; All restores all six with 'Showing 6 of 6 · All disciplines'.
The same Feature Finder block also renders on the About and Contact routes.
design_consistency: The Feature Finder reuses the Small Apps card treatment (white cards, soft shadow, #2e7eed accent, rounded pill tabs) and the six cards stay legible and non-overlapping.
The Small Apps content and visual system stay intact across the homepage and secondary routes.
regression: The homepage section set (hero, feature blocks, Feature Finder, video, testimonials, footer) remains intact.
The About, Contact and FAQ routes, the shared navigation, the contact form and the local imagery remain intact.
The desktop and tablet layouts remain coherent; no console pageerrors or failed network requests are introduced.
responsive: Mobile renders the homepage within the 390px viewport with no new horizontal scroll (the tab bar wraps and the card grid collapses).
Tablet and desktop layouts remain coherent and unchanged.

author_notes: Consistency / regression_continuity task (extend_interaction intent -> Consistency capability). The Small Apps homepage feature section is rebuilt into a NATIVE Feature Finder: an h2 'Find the right Small Apps feature', a .featfinder__bar of four discipline .featfinder__tab buttons (All/Design/Data/Workflow), a live .featfinder__readout, and a .featfinder__grid of six .featfinder__card tiles (Easy Prototyping, Art Direction, Sensor Bridge, Insight Charts, Strategist, Task Relay), each carrying data-featfinder-cat. The block is inserted identically (byte-for-byte) in every leg on the homepage and, for the reference, also on the About and Contact routes. Four orthogonal levers make this L4. D6 no_horizontal_overflow: the baseline keeps the original responsive defect (the filter bar is a fixed 760px non-wrapping row and the grid holds fixed min-width columns) so the finder region overflows a 390px phone by ~393px on mobile_home while the 1440px desktop and 834px tablet contain it; the reference wraps the bar and collapses the grid (grid-template-columns repeat with minmax(0,1fr), min-width:0) so mobile_home measures 0. D2 dom_assertions cross-page: the finder must render on About and Contact too — the baseline ships it on the homepage ONLY (fails About+Contact) and the bad leg ships it on the homepage and About but forgets Contact (fails Contact). D3 visual_regression: the bad leg's CSS pulls every card back over its neighbour with large negative margins (grid columns far wider than the container) so the six cards shingle into a single overlapping, colliding pile and recolours the cards to near-black text on a near-black slab so the headings and body copy are illegible and the readout is buried — a genuine geometry-and-contrast break over the whole finder region on the default desktop lever-state, not a tasteful recolour. D4 interaction_assertions: the bad leg's finder JS still re-filters the cards on click (the interaction registers) but snapshots the readout string once at init and only ever re-writes that frozen snapshot, so after clicking Data the grid shows two cards yet the readout stays 'Showing 6 of 6 · All disciplines' instead of 'Showing 2 of 6 · Data'. The reference and baseline share the correct filter JS, so the baseline passes D4 while failing D6+D3+D2 (strict-subset), and the bad leg fails all four. Infrastructure identical across legs (measurement-enabling, not graded): the remote Google Maps <script> and the remote Google Fonts @import are dropped so no offline network error fires; the template's overflow:hidden on the feature section and the global body{overflow-x:hidden} are neutralised so the mobile overflow is observable; AOS scroll transforms are pinned so the reference measures 0 phantom overflow. The three leg-varying files are css/style.css (the finder layout + the bad geometry break), js/finder.js (the correct vs frozen-readout filter wiring) and the per-route presence of the finder block; assets_to_consider stays disjoint from suggested_files. Local feature/logo imagery keeps the browser-visible asset-path signals; the design keywords covered include responsive layout, grid, mobile, card, filter and image.
